Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run-chase. The players are back in the middle. Megan Schutt has the ball in hand for Australia Women while Danni Wyatt-Hodge and Sophia Dunkley are the two English openers. Here we go!
…THE RUN CHASE…

England Women were much better with the ball as compared to the previous two T20Is and contained the runs to keep Australia Women under 165. They bowled as many as 15 overs of spin and it did help work for them. It was a collective bowling effort from the English Women where Linsey Smith, Freya Kemp, Charlie Dean, Sophie Ecclestone, and Alice Capsey all took one each. Right then, England Women need 163 to get their first win of the series. Heather Knight and her team will be confident of chasing this down but will have to bat well on this slowish wicket. Can they do it or will the Australian Women make a clean sweep in the T20Is as well? We shall find out. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Another solid batting effort from the Australian women helps them post a reasonable score of 162/5 from their 20 overs. Opting to bat first, Georgia Voll and Beth Mooney added a fifty-run stand for the first wicket. After Voll was dismissed on 23, Mooney made small partnerships with Phoebe Litchfield, Ellyse Perry, and Grace Harris and stuck some lovely shots as she carried her bat through the innings and finished with a sublime 94 off just 63 balls.

A single to end the innings! Tosses it full, in line with the stumps. Mooney shuffles across for the sweep but fails to connect. An appeal from Sophie Ecclestone was turned down. England Women go upstairs for the review. The replay shows an inside edge on the blade. The ball ricochets into the off-side for one. Beth Mooney ends on an unbeaten 94. Australia Women finish on 162/5.

The umpires are already out in the middle and the players of England Women then make their way out to the field of play amidst all the fireworks. England Women (Playing XI) - Danni Wyatt-Hodge, Sophia Dunkley, Alice Capsey (In for Maia Bouchier), Natalie Sciver-Brunt, Heather Knight (C), Amy Jones (WK), Freya Kemp, Charlie Dean, Sophie Ecclestone, Linsey Smith (In for Sarah Glenn), Lauren Filer (In for Lauren Bell).

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Georgia Voll, Beth Mooney (WK), Phoebe Litchfield, Ellyse Perry, Annabel Sutherland, Tahlia McGrath (C), Grace Harris, Georgia Wareham, Alana King, Megan Schutt, Darcie Brown (In for Kim Garth).
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favor of Australia Women and they will BAT first.

With the series already beyond their reach, England Women will aim to play fearless cricket and earn their first points of the tour. So, can England Women bounce back, or will Australia Women continue their winning streak? Let’s find out. Toss and team news coming up shortly.

On the other hand, England Women have struggled to find their rhythm. Despite showing glimpses of promise, they’ve been unable to turn these moments into wins. In the second T20I, they bowled well in the early stages but allowed Australia Women to accelerate in the latter part of the innings. During their chase, England Women improved on their previous performances, but a few quiet overs and disruptions from rain slowed their momentum, leaving them short of the target and visibly frustrated as well given it was their last chance of hoping to get on a winning run and draw the series.

Australian women have been dominant throughout the series and produced another strong performance in the previous match. In the second T20I, Australia Women posted a formidable total of 185, thanks to superb 40s from Beth Mooney and Tahlia McGrath and a cameo from Grace Harris. With solid bowling from Megan Schutt and Annabel Sutherland, they clinched a 6-run win in a rain-affected encounter via the DLS method. Heading into the third T20I, Australia Women will look to maintain their dominant form and extend their winning streak.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the third and final T20I in this multi-format Women's Ashes series between Australia Women and England Women at the Adelaide Oval. Australia Women have already secured an unassailable 10-0 lead, having retained the Ashes. England Women, who have yet to register a win on this tour, will be eager to claim a victory and salvage some pride in the remaining games.
... MATCH DAY ...

If dominance has a name, it’s Australia in this Women’s Ashes! After a ruthless ODI whitewash, the Aussies have wrapped up the T20I series with a game to spare, retaining the Ashes in style. The action now moves to the iconic Adelaide Oval for the third and final T20I. Despite missing regular skipper Alyssa Healy, their batting has been relentless. Beth Mooney has been sensational, scoring over 100 runs, including a classy 75 in the opener. Tahlia McGrath and Grace Harris have brought firepower in the middle, while Ellyse Perry, a proven match-winner, will be hungry to make a bigger impact. With rising stars like Georgia Voll and Phoebe Litchfield adding depth, the Aussies boast a batting lineup brimming with confidence. Annabel Sutherland’s all-round brilliance has been a key asset too. On the bowling front, spinners Alana King and Georgia Wareham have been exceptional, dismantling England’s batting in the first game. The pace duo of Megan Schutt and Kim Garth along with the others have complemented the spin department beautifully, maintaining the pressure throughout. Australia, as always, looks like a well-oiled machine ready to finish the series on a high. England Women, however, will feel the sting of missed opportunities, especially in the last game. Skipper Heather Knight's explosive 43 off 19 balls had kept them in the hunt, but rain had the final say, cutting short their chase and handing Australia a six-run win (DLS). Knight acknowledged the fairness of the decision but must wonder what could have been if she’d faced those last five deliveries. England’s biggest challenge has been inconsistency. Danni Wyatt-Hodge and Sophia Dunkley have shown flashes of brilliance, each scoring a fifty in the series, while Natalie Sciver-Brunt has been solid but needs to convert starts into match-defining innings. The pressure is on Maia Bouchier to step up at the top, while Amy Jones will need to unleash her finishing skills. With the ball, Lauren Bell and Freya Kemp lead the pace attack, while Sophie Ecclestone and Charlie Dean remain their trump cards in the spin department. Sarah Glenn, too, will want to make her mark in the final game. Can England salvage some pride and deny Australia a T20I clean sweep? Or will the Aussies complete their Ashes dominance with yet another clinical performance? Let’s find out soon!
